text:
elaine: Quick sync — trying to land a small spec + launch checklist for the Dedicated roadmap slice: balancing commitment velocity vs. burst experience (how smooth is the fallback when they exceed committed capacity).

sam: TL;DR: customers want predictable latency + ability to handle spikes without manual ops. We need to decide which compromise we accept first.

kevin: Customer voice: AcmePay said they'd sign if we guarantee <150ms p95 on committed throughput and soft burst for short spikes for 95% of requests. They're sensitive to billing complexity though.

maria: Operational constraints: autoscale cooldowns + prewarm aren't instantaneous. If we allow large soft bursts we risk capacity thrash or preempting other tenants. Need shaping rules.

nora: UX ask: admins want a single slider or profile to choose "commitment aggressiveness" (fast commit, low burst) vs "burst-friendly" (slower commit but higher short-term headroom). Can mock.

elaine: Proposal: ship a v1 with two knobs 1) Commitment Velocity (fast/standard/slow) controlling how quickly reserved capacity becomes active and billing proration; 2) Burst Bandwidth (none/soft/elastic) controlling immediate headroom and whether spillover triggers tenant-level throttles.

sam: Implementation notes: Commitment Velocity maps to workflow: fast = immediate allocation (higher risk of transient cold starts), standard = 1-hr ramp with prewarm budget, slow = scheduled start with guaranteed prewarm. Burst Bandwidth maps to routing: soft = allow X% over commit for T minutes with weighted backoff; elastic = allow on-demand if spare capacity across pool.

maria: Observability requirements: need token-level breakdown, per-tenant p95 under commit vs burst, and a new alert when burst spillover > 10% for 5m. Also record prewarm CPU/GPU usage for cost modeling.

kevin: Billing: customers asked for clear language. Suggest we bill committed capacity monthly, burst is metered by token-minute overage with caps. For soft bursts we can include a small free buffer for the first N minutes/day.

elaine: Launch criteria checklist draft: 
- API: endpoints for creating commitments with "velocity" and "burst_profile" fields
- Console: admin slider + breakdown UI (nora)
- Runtime: shaping policy + fallback routing (sam/maria)
- Billing: metering + cap defaults (kevin)
- Evals: run 3 customer regression prompt sets comparing quality/latency commit vs burst
- Docs: quickstart + FAQ on cost/latency tradeoffs

nora: UX question: do we show burst consumption in real-time (yes/no)? Customers asked for live telemetry during incidents. I vote yes with 30s refresh.

maria: We can expose a lightweight metric: burst_used_pct and burst_remaining_minutes. 30s is fine but watch cardinality.

sam: Tech risk: cross-tenant elastic bursts need global allocator changes. For v1 we should only allow elastic bursts within the same pool; global elastic can be v2.

kevin: Sales ask: can we offer a "trial burst" during onboarding to prove value? If so, we need safe limits (e.g., 10 minutes at soft profile) and auto-disable. Good sales tool.

elaine: Decision needed: do we prioritize fast commit UX (immediate activation) or robust burst shaping (lower risk to other tenants)? This drives infra work. Thoughts?

sam: My call: prioritize robust shaping first, because build vs incident cost is huge. Fast commit can be approximated by prewarm credits at signup.

kevin: Counterpoint: a few anchor customers signed because they could turn on capacity instantly. Losing that might cost deals. Could gate fast commit behind an eligibility check (enterprise only) to limit exposure.

maria: If we gate fast commit to enterprise we must add safeties: a default soft cap and auto-eviction policy if cluster pressure > 85%.

nora: Design-wise gating enterprise-only is okay — we can show a CTA to request fast activation and include a checklist for support to enable.

elaine: Action proposal: ship v1 with standard/slow commit publicly, enterprise fast-commit behind a feature flag and onboarding flow + prewarm credits, soft-burst included for standard profiles with conservative limits. Elastic burst limited to pool-local for v1.

sam: Tech plan (short):
- week 1: spec API fields + console mocks
- week 2–3: implement shaping enforcement + pool-local elastic allocator
- week 4: telemetry + alerts + billing hooks
- week 5: customer pilots (2 anchors)

kevin: I'll coordinate pilot customers and draft FAQ for sales. Need a sample SLA blurb for signed commitments.

maria: Ops: I'll add the alert rules and an oncall playbook for burst spillover. Also will run chaos tests (synthetic spikes) during week 4.

nora: I'll attach console mocks by EOD Wednesday and a short microcopy set for the CTA.

elaine: Acceptance criteria for GA:
- commit create/update API works + validated k8s prewarm jobs spin up as per velocity
- p95 latency under commit stays <150ms for pilot tenants; burst paths documented and observed
- billing reports show per-tenant burst usage and monthly cap enforcement
- console shows real-time burst usage and allows switching profiles (with guardrails)

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: feature-flagged rollout planned. Canary to 5% of traffic then 25% if no spike alerts for 2h.

sam: Risks to track: unfair preemption, cost blowouts, UI confusion, too many knobs. Team should finalize a minimal default config.

elaine: Minimal defaults suggestion: velocity=standard, burst_profile=soft with 10% headroom for up to 5 minutes/day free, overage billed thereafter, enterprise fast-commit opt-in.

kevin: Approved by sales for pilots. I'll start outreach.

maria: I'll start writing the playbook and add load tests to CI.

nora: Will upload mocks shortly.

elaine: Great — we'll reconvene Friday to lock the spec for the sprint. Thanks all :thumbsup:
